Rockstar described how insanely realistic the police system and NPC behavior are in GTA 6:

- If you’re wanted and hide inside a bus, police driving past won’t search it if they didn’t see you get on
- If you leave the wanted area, police have no logical reason to search the bus
- In GTA 5, police would simply spawn where you’re hiding and start searching, even if you leave the wanted area, which forces you to stay on the run
- If you want to rob a store full of NPCs, you can pick up fights with them, provoke them then immediately defuse the situation, and they’ll actually leave the store. This way you’ll have fewer witnesses
- The game’s systems are designed to behave logically and realistically

(via Edge Magazine)

GTA 6 is officially 20 days out from launch (under 3 weeks).

Pre-loading begins in less than 2 weeks ⏳

Rockstar brought back the iconic GTA 5 gameplay trailer narrator, Tish Hicks to present the GTA 6 clip in a collaboration with South Park.

Rob Nelson previously stated that the team avoided making a narrated trailer this time, due to the amount of stuff they wanted to show in the Extended Look, describing it as an extremely difficult game to show off.

Rockstar should make GTA 6 a global launch rather than midnight if they want as many people as possible to watch the Heat event (A Night in Vice City) on November 18, and also to prevent early spoilers.

Currently, anyone with a New Zealand account will have GTA 6 unlocked 13 hours before the event even begins, so social media will be flooded with people discussing it instead of the event.

However, a midnight rollout for pre-loading makes total sense to help balance server strain when everyone starts downloading, but the actual release should be synchronized globally since there’s currently no online mode.
